summary: WebSocket-driven PTY shell, file writes, and self-upgrade give the remote server full control of the installer host
details: On startup (via the `yeaft-agent` bin, `npm start`, or `require`), index.js opens a WebSocket to CONFIG.serverUrl (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL) and routes incoming messages through message-router.js to handlers that (a) spawn an interactive user shell with node-pty and pipe network-supplied bytes into `pty.write` on `terminal_input`, (b) read, write, and delete arbitrary files and run git operations on `write_file`/`delete_files`/`git_*`, and (c) run `npm install <pkg>@latest` on `upgrade_agent`. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket endpoint obtains arbitrary command execution, arbitrary filesystem read/write, and package-install-driven code execution on the host. Separately, on startup ensureYeaftSkills() performs `git clone https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git` (or `git pull --ff-only`) into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev at mutable HEAD, chmods hooks 0755, and writes ~/.claude/settings.json to enable the plugin — an unpinned same-publisher code-fetch that auto-activates in the Claude CLI on every launch.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
